events.title: Dallas midterm convention nationalizes the race
events.detail: Trump tells voters to treat the midterms as if he were on the ballot; vulnerable Republicans face a localize-vs-nationalize trade-off.

events.title: Trump proposes a conditional $5,000 adult payment
events.detail: Confirmed campaign promise; funding and legislative path remain unresolved. Track fiscal and voter-response effects separately.

events.title: DNC targets conservative YouTube audiences on affordability
events.detail: Counter-programming around the GOP convention reinforces lower-costs / healthcare / housing as the Democratic national frame.

events.title: Missouri map fight returns to the U.S. Supreme Court
events.detail: One district can matter because the House majority margin is extremely narrow.

events.title: Administration renews Supreme Court bid on mail-voting rule
events.detail: Voting-administration litigation becomes a direct election-process variable as ballots begin moving.

events.title: FEC 60-day electioneering-communications window begins
events.detail: 24-hour disclosure requirements make ad spending and sponsor behavior more observable into Election Day.

money.headline: Money is the GOP's clearest structural counterweight to the national environment.
facts: Supreme Court preserved access to discounted broadcast rates for party committees.
Reuters reported a large national-committee resource advantage for Republicans in the related litigation.
MAGA Inc. is deploying major resources into Texas, signaling that the seat is not being treated as safely Republican.

market_readthrough.logic: Oil/inflation + election-linked fiscal promises can lift term premium; divided government can offset through gridlock.
Higher U.S. yields support USD; political/fiscal risk and weaker growth can work the other way.
Oil is not merely an asset outcome; it is an input into approval, inflation and turnout.
War, fiscal uncertainty and institutional conflict strengthen hedging demand.
War duration and post-election congressional composition affect authorization and oversight.
A Democratic Congress raises oversight risk; executive deregulation can continue under divided government.
Affordability politics can pull subsidies, drug costs and insurance policy into the center.
Tax-credit durability and appropriations depend more on chamber control than campaign rhetoric.
Market-structure legislation and oversight intensity depend on committee control.
AI regulation, grid bills, power infrastructure and data-center politics are becoming local election inputs.

delta.headline: T-54 baseline established
items: House: Democratic-favored in prediction markets; Cook still shows a narrow structural battlefield.
Senate: genuine toss-up after Texas and Iowa moved into the top competitive tier.
National frame: affordability is dominant; Iran → oil → inflation is the highest-value cross-domain transmission chain.
Campaign strategy: GOP is nationalizing around Trump while Democrats are localizing pain around prices and turnout.
